headlineOfDay: Fears over the cost of the AI boom drove a sell-off of close to $1tn in US tech stocks, with Intel suffering its worst day since the 1970s, while Brent crude neared $120 on renewed Hormuz attacks.

markets.summary: Wall Street fell sharply on Friday as disappointing earnings deepened doubts about whether heavy AI spending will pay off. The Nasdaq lost 2.86% and the S&P 500 1.82%, with Intel, Reddit and Google among the heaviest casualties. The FTSE 100 was broadly flat, while Brent rose 2.4% to $117.64 and gold fell to its lowest level in a year.

indices.label: Nasdaq
indices.note: Fell 2.86% as concerns over AI spending and disappointing tech earnings fuelled a broad sell-off.

commodities.label: Gold
commodities.note: Fell to its lowest price in a year despite jitters over possible fresh Middle East attacks.

commodities.label: Brent crude
commodities.note: Rose towards $120 after a tanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz amid fears of renewed US-Iran hostilities.

losers.name: Reddit
losers.note: Biggest one-day drop on record after it reported a significant fall in search referral traffic in the third quarter.

losers.name: Intel
losers.note: Weak PC demand caused by high memory-chip prices, plus a struggle to make enough AI server chips.

stories.headline: Tech rout wipes almost $1tn off US stocks
stories.summary: A tech sell-off that began earlier in the month gathered pace after subpar earnings, as investors questioned whether the billions being spent on AI can generate returns quickly enough. Some commentators are drawing parallels with the peak of the dot-com bubble, and others are urging investors to diversify into consumer stocks.
